html:
In May 1655 an English fleet sent by Oliver Cromwell seized Jamaica from Spain. The expedition had failed to take Santo Domingo, its first target, and took the lightly held island instead.

The Spanish freed or abandoned their enslaved Africans, many of whom fled to the mountains and became the Maroons. Spain gave up its claim in the Treaty of Madrid of 1670.

England first used the island as a base for buccaneers at Port Royal, led by men like Henry Morgan. Then planters from Barbados brought sugar and enslaved Africans on a huge scale. By the 1700s Jamaica was Britain's most valuable colony in the Caribbean, worked by hundreds of thousands of enslaved people.
